findings.claim: Section 1 baseline (17.2 m/s tip at 0.29 s, order elbow->wrist->waist->pelvis, 32 J) describes today's cut; stage-0 gate requires these numbers to reappear.
findings.problem: The probe scene is in a state that never occurs in play. probe.mjs writes handOffset directly on the harness 'player' with autoGuard false, handHeld/inputActive false and no aiCtl. So (a) the cut starts with rest weight idle=1, i.e. the guard-table coil (chest -45 deg, pelvis -17.5 deg), whereas in play a touching finger or an AI in attack mode holds idleGoal=0 (chest only about -8 to -17 deg); (b) when 'swinging' drops at 0.175 s, idleGoal jumps back to 1 (cutPending && canRecover is false without autoGuard) and a second trunk/hand/blade command toward the left-Wechsel table pose starts in the last 110 ms before tip peak. The late pelvis peak (0.19 s) that carries the 'reversed order' diagnosis may be partly this artefact. The stage-0 gate would lock the artefact into the dojo scene. coil (#12) also depends on this state.
findings.evidence: wt_r9 src/skill.js:1864 (idleGoal), :201 and :1781 (autoGuard false -> canRecover false), :179-182 (aiFingerHeld); tools/sim/harness_m.mjs newRound sets no autoGuard; $S/p2/r11/probe.mjs. Kinematic replay of the command chain (no physics): $S/p2/r11/review/cmd_chain3.mjs -> probe scene: chest command 0.17 rad at 0.175 s -> 0.45 at 0.29 s -> 0.62 at 0.45 s, pelvis 0.10 -> 0.20 -> 0.245; play-like (idle stays 0): chest 0.17 -> 0.31 -> 0.30, pelvis 0.10 -> 0.14 -> 0.125. Would settle it: rerun the probe once with corr_lib-style finger input (handHeld, inputActive, autoGuard true) and once driven by real ai.js attack, and compare order and peak.
findings.fix: Re-measure every baseline (probe, honesty stroke, hard-line baselines) under the two real input paths before any threshold is derived; delete the 'section 1 numbers reappear' gate; the dojo scene must drive the finger pump and ai.js (or set the same flags), not raw handOffset.

findings.claim: The trunk follows aimRaw and leads the hand; handDelay lets the arm lag; carry (0..1) makes the trunk's lead ride into the hand while the end position stays the same.
findings.problem: Three code facts break this. (1) Most of the swing's trunk rotation is the arc term, and it is driven by the FILTERED hand aim times activity, not aimRaw: arc = -sk.aim.x * trunkArc * act * 0.35, about 2.6x the aimRaw term at trunkArc 2; applyPose adds another (1-s) share from sk.aim.x. So handDelay delays most of the trunk command together with the hand, and raising trunkArc only enlarges a term that trails the hand (matches the probe: 17.2 -> 17.3 m/s). (2) carry as defined is net-zero and negative near contact. At defaults the lead angle is negative the whole stroke (min -0.30 rad at 0.09 s), so carry alone holds the hand back; the stage-2 gate 'carry raises trunk share by 5 points' would pass by slowing the arm, the design's own cheat #15. With handDelay 0.08 the lead rises to +0.26 rad at 0.117 s and falls to -0.05 by 0.25 s, i.e. carry subtracts about 2.4 rad/s x carry from the hand command during the 130 ms before contact. Because the lead must return to zero, mid-path gain is always paid back at the end. (3) There is no carry for pitch at all: the hand target is chest position + heading-yaw frame, so trunk flexion (the proximal motion that matters in a cut that is 85 % downward) is undone by the arm. Also the lead is not zero at rest unless the reference includes the rest-weight/table blend and every overlay (thrust, finish, okori, uniq, ex), and it leaves +0.03 rad at 0.5 s.
findings.evidence: wt_r9 src/fighter.js:1432 (arc from sk.aim.x), :1452-1453, :3221 ((1-s) term), :3614 (handTarget = handLocal rotated by this.yaw + chest translation), :3698. Numbers from $S/p2/r11/review/cmd_chain2.mjs (command chain only, s 0.7, 12 m/s). Would settle it: pair sweep carry x handDelay reporting hand-target velocity at the contact instant, not trunk share.
findings.fix: Before training: drive arc from aimRaw (or from the same delayed chest command), and express hand target and blade aim in a frame that follows the commanded chest yaw AND pitch (the s2 structure the design postpones). Keep 'end pose unchanged' by evaluating the table at the end pose, not by forcing the lead back to zero before contact.

findings.claim: pelvisRate (15..60 rad/s) and chestDelay let the hips start first; hard line 3 (declared aid <= baseline) keeps it honest.
findings.problem: The pelvis command already leads (command peak 0.050 s, chest 0.083 s, hand 0.092 s); the body's pelvis peaks at 0.19 s at about half the commanded rate. The bottleneck is the leg yaw controller, which the program does not touch: torque clamp +-100 N*m (LEGS.yawMax), feed-forward rate clamp +-6 rad/s, feedback rate cap sqrt(2*15*err), and in single stance (during any passing step) soft gains 60/20 with only about 26 N*m of foot twist from the ground. The baseline already drives declared yaw aid to its 100 N*m cap, and hard line 3 forbids more, so the only remaining routes are stance width / foot loading (explicitly excluded from the program) and timing into double support. Yaw budget by hand: trunk+arms+sword about 4.6 kg*m^2; the design's hoped 4.5 rad/s at contact needs about 21 N*m*s, i.e. 0.21 s at the full 100 N*m, and about 42 N*m*s including stopping, against a per-cut aid allowance of 11.8. The expected +2.7 m/s from yaw is not supported. Twist room is also short: the rest coil already uses 27.5 of the 45 deg spine limit (38.5 at coil 1.4), so chestDelay and coil compete for 17 deg.
findings.evidence: wt_r9 src/fighter.js:2998-3006 (yaw intent, rate clamp +-6), src/legs_vmc.js:544-556 (yaw law, comment '26 N*m one foot, about 90 two feet'), src/config.js LEGS yawK 500 / yawD 45 / yawMax 100 / yawKs 60 / yawDs 20 / yawDecel 15, limit.hipRot 70; src/fighter.js:3222 (twist clamp +-0.8), :157 (spineTwist +-45). Command timing from cmd_chain2.mjs; body timing from the design's own table. Would settle it: per cut, log demanded yaw torque, ground-delivered part and remainder (legDrive.rem) through the stroke.
findings.fix: Make pelvis yaw authority the first thing measured in stage 0. Either add the excluded degrees of freedom (stance width, foot angle, weight split before the cut) or state the ceiling and lower the success targets.

findings.claim: Rows blend in by stroke direction (pad velocity, +-35 deg) and skill.activity; a stroke without a trained row is unchanged; no switch.
findings.problem: True only until one row exists. activity goes to 1 for ANY pad motion above 1.5 m/s: AI parries (parrySpeed 3.5-5.5 m/s, the code comment itself says they are read as swings), AI chamber moves (2.2-3.8 m/s), the human parry button (guardDrive), finger guard changes, and thrusts (activity = max(activity, thrustPose.w)). Every such motion whose direction falls in the cone gets the trained handDelay/wristDelay/reachDelay (up to 0.12 + 0.12 s) at full weight. A high-right to low-left parry would arrive 0.1-0.24 s late. None of these motions is in the practice set; the first place it can show is parry_gap_map after the overnight run, and fixing the gating then invalidates the trained numbers. Delays are also absolute seconds applied to strokes of any length (a 0.3 m swipe at 12 m/s is a 25 ms command).
findings.evidence: wt_r9 src/skill.js:1682, :1693-1697 (fast = swinging || guardDrive; activity time constants 0.04 up / 0.4 down), :1876; src/config.js AI_LEVELS parrySpeed/chamberSpeed, SKILL.swingSpeed 1.5. Would settle it: fingerprint of a scripted parry and a chamber move through the cone with the row installed vs not.
findings.fix: Weight must also depend on something that separates a cut from a parry or chamber without a switch (for example a smooth ramp on command speed between the parry band and the strike band, plus stroke length), and 'parry / chamber / thrust trajectories unchanged' must be a hard line measured in practice, not only at stage 6.

findings.claim: handRate, stepDelay, stepLen, stepT, stepPush, shiftAmp, shiftT, pitchAmp, dropAmp, pulseRate, trunkFollow and coil are free numbers of the program.
findings.problem: Each is overridden or clamped by code outside the table. handRate (aimFilterStrike) applies only while 'swinging' (0 to 0.175 s for a 12 m/s stroke); after that the filter slides to SKILL.aimFilter 14, which is not in the program. handDelay pushes the hand out of that window: hand-command peak speed 8.4 -> 7.8 (0.08 s) -> 6.0 m/s (0.12 s). Step numbers are requests: duration clamped to 0.28-0.7 s, refused while the stick is pulled back (AI holds -0.21 when not stepping), lift can wait up to GAIT.liftWait 0.4 s, a different foot may be put down first, the landing spot is moved toward the capture point, body follow is cut at legVmax 1.1 m/s, schools convert pass to lunge, and AI has other paths (school cutStep, tech.step, thrust lunge). shiftAmp goes through the stick: goAccel 1.5 m/s^2 gives at most 0.45 m/s by contact. pitch/drop pulses exist only while the pad moves (0.1 s), then pass 2-3 cascaded followers and a height loop of 11 rad/s (0.1 s pulse -> 0.59 of amplitude after the first filter alone); expected '+1.5-2 m/s from lean and drop' looks 3-5x too high. trunkFollow acts only while aimLagBehind > 0 and swingDir is set. coil is multiplied in by a weight that is zero at rest, so as specified it does nothing while waiting, and in play the table coil is absent anyway (idle 0). Step numbers are read once at stroke start, when the weight is about 0.2; the formula 'default + w x (row - default)' is undefined for event-read values. chestRate shares SKILL_BODY.chest with the rest-weight and pitch followers, so it also retimes hand and blade blending.
findings.evidence: wt_r9 src/skill.js:1735-1737; src/gait.js:436-455, :1296-1320, :1423, :1436, :2152-2166; src/config.js GAIT liftWait 0.4 / goAccel 1.5 / legVmax 1.1 / maxAccel 3.2, LEGS heightK 9000 / heightD 900; src/ai.js:4517-4531, :4671-4697; src/fighter.js:1436, :1507, :1516-1519. Figures from cmd_chain.mjs and budget.mjs in $S/p2/r11/review/.
findings.fix: For each program number list the code clamp next to it and either move the clamp's constant into the table or drop the number. Tie the 'fast' window to the delayed command. Say which weight event-read values use. Key coil by guard, or remove it.

findings.claim: The step numbers (#17-22) let the legs lead; success = foot plant within +-50 ms of contact and legs+pelvis+waist share above 20 %.
findings.problem: The legs cannot lead in this structure and cannot add blade energy in this cut. Clock zero is the stroke command and stepDelay >= 0, minimum flight is 0.28 s, so the earliest plant is about 0.28 s against a baseline contact near 0.29 s. The only probe variant where the foot was down in time asked for the step 0.18 s BEFORE the stroke (probe.mjs stepLead: -0.18; the text says 0.13), which is outside the range 0..0.15 and against 'nothing moves before the command'. The plant moved only 0.12 s for 0.18 s of lead, so the gait's own wait already varies. Getting the foot down before the hips turn therefore requires delaying the blade by 0.1-0.2 s, which the owner already rejected as dull at +183 ms. Geometry: the blade's direction at peak is 0.85 down and 0.53 sideways, so the forward share is 0 to 0.1; a body moving forward at 1 m/s adds under 1 % to blade speed. Six of the 23 numbers cannot move the energy term by more than 1-3 %; the 20 % share must come from pelvis yaw and waist alone.
findings.evidence: wt_r9 src/gait.js:441 (clamp 0.28), probe.mjs VARS.stepLead, design table section 1-1 and 1-2; budget.mjs (forward share sqrt(1 - 0.85^2 - 0.53^2) = 0.00 to 0.10).
findings.fix: For AI, request the step during wind-up (the AI knows it will strike; that is a real negative delay). For the human path accept 'hand before foot' and say so. Remove leg push from the energy expectation, or choose a first motion where proximal motion lines up with the blade: a horizontal cut (yaw share 1.0) or a lunge-thrust (finish_thrust.mjs exists; legs add directly along the tip).

findings.claim: A trained cut generalises to play; the real-body check at stage 6 confirms it.
findings.problem: Two timers outside the program cut a delayed stroke short in play but not in the dojo, which watches 0.7 s. AI: when the pad path ends the AI enters 'follow' with timer 0.3 s, then afterStrike changes mode (hand target jumps, rest weight returns). Pad ends at 0.084-0.147 s, so the window closes at 0.38-0.45 s; with contact allowed at baseline + 80 ms (0.37 s) the margin is 14-30 ms, and the fast and firm presets have no delay bound. Human: recovery starts 0.25 s after the finger stops (about 0.35 s after start for a 0.1 s swipe); delayed hand and blade then read a history that already contains the return. Also the dojo's scripted return to the roof guard at 2 m/s is itself a 'swing' by the code (above 1.5 m/s), while the game returns at 1.2 m/s to the home guard, so the recovery term is measured on a motion play never makes. Training never runs ai.js or the finger pump, so neither real code path is exercised until stage 6.
findings.evidence: wt_r9 src/ai.js:2079-2085 (follow timer 0.3), src/config.js SKILL.recoverDelay 0.25, recoverSpeed 1.2, swingSpeed 1.5; src/skill.js:1784-1841.
findings.fix: Put both timers in the scene as they are in play (drive the cut through ai.js and through the finger pump with autoGuard), or list them as coupled constants the owner must see. Measure recovery with the game's own recovery.

findings.claim: Hard line 3 (per-cut yaw aid integral <= baseline, external work share <= 6.6 %) closes the biggest hole, the declared external aid.
findings.problem: It bounds the wrong quantities. The aid is an external torque on the pelvis; the score counts blade energy whatever its source. An integral of |torque| equal to the baseline (11.8 N*m*s standing, 18.9 stepping) can be re-timed into the acceleration phase: 100 N*m for 0.12 s is 11.8 N*m*s of free angular impulse, the same order as the whole swing's yaw angular momentum (roughly 10-21 N*m*s). The work line is a ratio, so aid work can grow with muscle work; baseline aid work is already 28.8 J against 32 J of real blade energy. A candidate can keep both lines and be mostly aid-powered. Tilt aid (cap 80) has the same shape.
findings.evidence: wt_r9 src/fighter.js:2858-2892 (driveAid adds torque to the pelvis), design section 1-3 (peak 100.0, added work 28.8 J) and section 5-2 line 3. Would settle it: per cut, signed aid work and signed yaw impulse in the stroke direction from command start to contact, baseline vs candidate.
findings.fix: Bound, in absolute units, the positive aid work and the aid angular impulse in the stroke direction before contact; report blade energy net of external work; add tolerance from measured baseline noise.

findings.claim: Hard line 2 keeps joint torques human: per joint, share of steps over the referee limit <= baseline, 95th percentile <= max(baseline, limit).
findings.problem: (1) The wrist is grandfathered at 28.4 % of steps over limit (peak 58 vs 25 N*m) and delivers 66 % of tip speed. The 95th-percentile rule leaves the top 5 % of a 240-step cycle free: 12 steps = 100 ms = the whole release. The score is 0.5 x free-sword mass x v^2 and shares are not scored, so the cheapest gain is better wrist timing (wristDelay, releaseMargin). The likely outcome is a more wrist-driven cut, the opposite of the owner's aim, and the honest-wrist run comes only at stage 8 after he has chosen among three previews built on the dishonest wrist. (2) Shares are diluted over a 2 s cycle of which 0.3 s is stroke. (3) Referee limits are one scalar per joint: waist 300, hip 250. The axes this optimisation loads are axial: trunk twist (human roughly 100-150 N*m, from memory, unverified) and hip rotation (the game's own LEGS.limit.hipRot is 70). The waist is an engine motor with unbounded damping torque and no force-velocity law; hard line 9 allows 12 rad/s against today's 6.5. Expect the gain to be routed through waist twist.
findings.evidence: /home/user/halfsword/tools/sim/honesty.mjs:120-121 (HUMAN table, scalar per joint); wt_r9 src/fighter.js:124-125 (abdomen/chest k 1800/1600, max 500/440), :3251-3284 (target clamp limits only the spring part), :3877-3917 (wrist cap). Would settle it: split delivered waist and hip torque by axis in the ledger for the baseline cut.
findings.fix: Train the honest-wrist variant first or alongside; window the torque line on command start to contact + 0.2 s; add axial limits for waist twist and hip rotation.

findings.claim: Seventeen cheats are listed and caught; hard constraints are measurable per rollout.
findings.problem: Gaps specific to this simulator. (a) No line for sword-on-ground: the sword collides with the ground and the cut ends low-left, so a late brake can bounce off the floor or prop the body; cheap to detect. (b) The fighter's own sword does not collide with its own shins, feet or off arm (only torso and thighs), so a follow-through may pass through the lead leg for free. (c) Ledger-only lines (delivered torque, solver-given energy) are checked on the top three every 10 generations; demoting them afterwards cannot undo ten generations of distribution update, so the ledger filters the report, it does not constrain the search. (d) '<= baseline' lines have no noise margin: the start point sits on four or five constraint boundaries at once, so with initial step 0.25 most of the first population is infeasible and ranking by violation pulls toward calmer (slower) motion. (e) A catch step costs 2 points while +10 % energy pays 4 in the 'loaded' preset: the optimiser will buy energy with stumbles. (f) Blade point travels 0.118 m per step against a 0.12 m target radius; a point-in-sphere test at step times aliases on grazing passes. (g) Energy uses speed relative to a moving target, crediting the target's own 0.5-1.0 m/s. (h) Who aims the fixed pad path at a randomised target is not specified; a miss is worth -40 points against +12 for the whole success target, so the score is dominated by hit/miss and reach, not sequence. (i) The last cut of each 4-cut episode has no next cut to pay for lost balance. (j) The edge-alignment window (corr.js) needs an opponent body part, so alignment in the dojo runs a different path than in play.
findings.evidence: wt_r9 src/self_contact.js:24-49 (weapon vs ground collides; same-fighter pairs dropped except torso-weapon and torso-arm); src/corr.js header; design sections 4-1, 5-2, 5-4, 6-1; budget.mjs (14.2/120 = 0.118 m).
findings.fix: Add hard lines: sword-ground contact steps = 0 and a geometric blade-vs-own-leg clearance; run the ledger on each generation's elite (about +40 % cost) or validate cheap proxies in stage 0; set margins from an A/A run of the baseline; swept contact test; world-frame blade speed; specify aiming; add a 1 s tail after the last cut.

findings.claim: Fall is a hard line ('0 falls'); success includes 'fewer than 1 fall per 100 whiffs' and 'self-falls in 24 AI fights not worse'.
findings.problem: The sample sizes cannot see it. With a 3 % fall chance per cut, 8 cuts show no fall 78 % of the time and the 32-cut check 38 %. Zero falls in 300 cuts only bounds the rate at 1.0 % (95 %), so the criterion fails on one fall and cannot be compared with a baseline. In fights the recorded baseline is about 22 self-falls per 24 fights: one-sigma is +-21 %, and a two-arm difference needs 60 % to reach two sigma. Every dojo cut is a whiff with no blade contact and no opponent, while in-fight falls come from contact and being pushed, so selection pressure toward the stability edge is invisible until stage 6, and stage 6 cannot resolve it.
findings.evidence: budget.mjs output; wt_r9 src/config.js:785 (24 fights: 23 never-fell bodies, 22 self-falls at aid 100/80).
findings.fix: About 200+ fights per arm (roughly 90 core-minutes at 1.67 ms/step) or paired seeds for the fight gate; add a contact scene (standing dummy body, blocked blade) to practice; treat capture-point excursions beyond baseline as a hard line rather than a score term.

findings.claim: Shares (legs/trunk percentage) are read-only results measured with chain.mjs; stage 6 requires fight chain, wounds and the other referees to be 'not worse'.
findings.problem: Two referee readings move for reasons that are not the body's doing. (1) chain.mjs in fights takes the fastest tip moment only while skill.swinging is true. For AI strokes that window is about 0 to 0.18 s, while the true peak is near 0.29 s; that is why fights read 8-10 m/s and the solo probe 17 m/s (the design gives a different reason). With any handDelay the arm has not started inside that window, so the fight 'legs/trunk share' rises by construction. (2) Judged damage adds STRIKE.stepMass 1.0 kg (on top of 0.32 free + 0.3 arm) when the pelvis is still approaching at contact. Today's AI lands the foot 0.13 s after tip peak and collects it; a better ordered cut (plant, then cut) loses it. So 'wounds not worse' can fail for a real improvement and pass for none.
findings.evidence: /home/user/halfsword/docs/strike/physics2_proto/r9/chain.mjs (decomposition gated on f.skill.swinging); cmd_chain.mjs (swinging on 0.000-0.175 s); wt_r9 src/combat.js:113-126, :352-360; src/config.js STRIKE.stepMass 1.0, energyScale 2.0. Would settle it: log tip speed for 0.3 s after swinging ends in a fight.
findings.fix: Fix the chain window (peak within command start + 0.6 s) before it is used as a yardstick; report share by joint work at contact; state that stage 6 judges on physical energy and that judged damage is reported, not gated, until the owner decides section 12-3.

findings.claim: One training run is about 40 min on 4 free cores or 1.5 h under load; first motion 3.5-8 h; 20-24 individuals x 120-150 generations are enough.
findings.problem: The arithmetic checks on free cores (2,400 steps + 0.3 s = 2.6 s per evaluation; 3,600 evaluations = 39 min; table total 3.5 h). But: the table counts the standing stage once while gate 4 needs three restarts, and the three presets are not counted for it: 4.8 h on 4 free cores, 6.4 h with 3 workers, 11 h at 1.75 ms. Adding 3 workers to a 4-core machine already at load 7 gives about 2.4 ms/step, i.e. 11-15 h, not one night. Covariance learning time constant is about 51 generations at n=23, population 24 (35 at n=17, population 20), with 276 covariance terms; 150 generations is about three time constants: enough for a first-order gain, not enough to trust 'the numbers are entangled' or agreement between restarts. Ten of the 17 standing-stage numbers start exactly on the lower wall; with reflection at the wall the fitness is even in those coordinates and the mean cannot move unless the repaired points are fed back into the update. The sweep compares 212 candidates against a 5 % threshold on 16 cuts each with noise not yet measured; some will pass by chance, so the early-failure alarm can stay silent on an inert structure.
findings.evidence: $S/p2/r11/review/budget.mjs (budget table, c1 0.00335, cmu 0.01636 for n=23). The 2.4 ms figure is my estimate from load share, not measured.
findings.fix: Budget the restarts and presets; measure A/A noise in stage 0 and confirm sweep winners on fresh seeds; feed repaired points back or start the new numbers inside the box; add wall-optimum and wall-start cases to the stage-3 test functions.

findings.claim: Hand-setting is ruled out because the numbers are entangled; 23 numbers need an evolution strategy overnight.
findings.problem: A simpler path likely gives most of the gain and tests the structure in minutes. From the code reading, most of the 23 are inert or clamped (above); the live levers are few: wrist release (wristDelay, releaseMargin), hand lag (handRate, handDelay), trunk amplitude and its carry. The design's own evidence for entanglement is one hand-made combination whose ingredients include a lever now shown to trail the hand (trunkArc). A 5x5x5 grid over three numbers with 32 cuts each is 4,000 cuts = 960k steps, about 4 minutes on 4 free cores (about 10 under load), gives full response surfaces, the noise level and readable numbers for the owner.
findings.evidence: budget arithmetic: 4,000 x 240 x 0.96 ms / 4 = 230 s. Would settle it: after the structural fixes, if the grid shows a ridge that three numbers cannot follow, bring in the strategy.
findings.fix: Order: (1) structural fixes by hand, each checked with the play-like probe: arc from aimRaw, hand in chest frame, AI step in wind-up, 'fast' tied to the delayed command; (2) four timings set from biomechanics: pelvis to chest 30-40 ms, chest to hand 50-70 ms, hand to wrist release 40-60 ms, foot down 50-100 ms before contact (ranges from memory, unverified); (3) grid two or three numbers. Keep the evolution strategy for balance reflexes, where feedback gains do interact.

findings.claim: Every new value defaults to today's number, so there is no switch and the default tree is bit-identical.
findings.problem: Checked per change. Holds exactly: table blend at weight 0 (x + 0*(y-x) = x), delays at 0 if the newest slot is read without arithmetic, carry 0 (rotation by 0 is exact), coil 1, pulse amplitude 0, pelvisShare 0.5 moved to the table (note other literal 0.5 pelvis shares stay in the overlay lines). Does not hold: the leg numbers have two different 'today' values in one cell (AI 0.04 s / 0.6 m / 0.4 s / stick 1; human 0 s / 0.3 m / 0.3 s / 0.9 x level, and only when the foe is 1.3-2.4 m away), so a single default changes one side or keeps a branch on aiControlled; the design flags this as an owner question but the summary still says 'all'. The three presets are separate builds, which is fine. Delay buffers are in step slots while tired fighters run the command clock slower (attackSpeed), so delays in seconds do not scale with a stretched stroke.
findings.fix: State the leg defaults as two rows until section 12-6 is decided, and exclude #17-22 from the 'bit-identical' claim.
